question: What geographic feature primarily controls the eastern boundary of the Indian Desert?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aravalli Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **eastern boundary of the Indian Desert**, also known as the Thar Desert, is primarily controlled by the **Aravalli Hills**, which act as a natural barrier limiting the desert's expansion eastward.
 
• The **Aravalli Range** is one of the world's oldest mountain ranges, dating back to the **Precambrian Era**, and runs in a **northeast-southwest direction** across the states of Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat, and Delhi.
 
• The Aravalli Hills contribute to the **geographical and climatic delineation** of the region by intercepting the southwestern monsoon winds and reducing their moisture content, which affects the arid conditions of the Thar Desert.</li
